introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics Paper 2 (0765/2), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2021. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
incertitudes: Question 10 (b) : le sujet imprime les mêmes 9 marks pour « find the inverse » et « hence solve » ; un seul bloc (sous-question b) est donc conservé. questions.enonce_markdown: Find the value of the constant $k$ for which the matrix $\mathbf{A}$ is singular, where $\mathbf{A} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 5 & 0 & k \end{pmatrix}$. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A square matrix is singular exactly when its determinant is zero. Expand along the first row:

$$\det\mathbf{A} = 2\bigl[(-1)(k) - (2)(0)\bigr] - 3\bigl[(1)(k) - (2)(5)\bigr] + 4\bigl[(1)(0) - (-1)(5)\bigr] = -2k - 3k + 30 + 20 = 50 - 5k.$$

$\det\mathbf{A} = 0 \Rightarrow 50 - 5k = 0$.

$$\boxed{k = 10}$$

questions.enonce_markdown:
Find the inverse of matrix $\mathbf{B}$, if $\mathbf{B} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 5 & 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$. Hence solve the system of equations

$$\begin{cases} 2x + 3y + 4z = 1, \\ x - y + 2z = 2, \\ 5x + 2z = 5. \end{cases}$$

(9 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Determinant.** $\det\mathbf{B} = 2\bigl[(-1)(2) - (2)(0)\bigr] - 3\bigl[(1)(2) - (2)(5)\bigr] + 4\bigl[(1)(0) - (-1)(5)\bigr] = -4 + 24 + 20 = 40 \neq 0$, so $\mathbf{B}$ is invertible. (This is $\det\mathbf{A}$ of part (a) with $k = 2$: $50 - 10 = 40$.)

**Cofactors** $C_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j} M_{ij}$:

$C_{11} = (-1)(2) - (2)(0) = -2$, $\quad C_{12} = -\bigl[(1)(2) - (2)(5)\bigr] = 8$, $\quad C_{13} = (1)(0) - (-1)(5) = 5$,

$C_{21} = -\bigl[(3)(2) - (4)(0)\bigr] = -6$, $\quad C_{22} = (2)(2) - (4)(5) = -16$, $\quad C_{23} = -\bigl[(2)(0) - (3)(5)\bigr] = 15$,

$C_{31} = (3)(2) - (4)(-1) = 10$, $\quad C_{32} = -\bigl[(2)(2) - (4)(1)\bigr] = 0$, $\quad C_{33} = (2)(-1) - (3)(1) = -5$.

The adjugate is the transpose of the cofactor matrix:

$$\operatorname{adj}\mathbf{B} = \begin{pmatrix} -2 & -6 & 10 \\ 8 & -16 & 0 \\ 5 & 15 & -5 \end{pmatrix}.$$

$$\boxed{\mathbf{B}^{-1} = \frac{1}{40}\begin{pmatrix} -2 & -6 & 10 \\ 8 & -16 & 0 \\ 5 & 15 & -5 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -\frac{1}{20} & -\frac{3}{20} & \frac14 \\ \frac15 & -\frac25 & 0 \\ \frac18 & \frac38 & -\frac18 \end{pmatrix}}$$

**Check:** first row of $\mathbf{B}$ times first column of $\operatorname{adj}\mathbf{B}$: $2(-2) + 3(8) + 4(5) = 40$; first row of $\mathbf{B}$ times second column: $2(-6) + 3(-16) + 4(15) = -12 - 48 + 60 = 0$.

**Solving the system.** In matrix form $\mathbf{B}\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$, so

$$\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix} = \mathbf{B}^{-1}\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{40}\begin{pmatrix} -2 - 12 + 50 \\ 8 - 32 + 0 \\ 5 + 30 - 25 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{40}\begin{pmatrix} 36 \\ -24 \\ 10 \end{pmatrix}.$$

$$\boxed{x = \frac{9}{10},\quad y = -\frac35,\quad z = \frac14}$$

**Check in the equations:** $2(0.9) + 3(-0.6) + 4(0.25) = 1.8 - 1.8 + 1 = 1$; $\ 0.9 + 0.6 + 0.5 = 2$; $\ 5(0.9) + 2(0.25) = 4.5 + 0.5 = 5$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the image of the point $\begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$ under the transformation matrix defined by $\mathbf{B}$. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The image of a point with position vector $\mathbf{p}$ under the transformation with matrix $\mathbf{B}$ is $\mathbf{B}\mathbf{p}$:

$$\begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 5 & 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -4 + 9 + 4 \\ -2 - 3 + 2 \\ -10 + 0 + 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 9 \\ -3 \\ -8 \end{pmatrix}.$$

$$\boxed{\text{The image is the point } (9,\ -3,\ -8)}$$
